---
title: LogitTilt
llms-description: LogitTilt raises how often a target model produces the behaviour under audit while keeping its output on-policy, so an auditor finds usable examples in fewer attempts.
---

## Overview

[LogitTilt](https://github.com/AdrSkapars/inspect_logittilt) makes a target model more
likely to produce the behaviour an audit is looking for, without pushing it off its own
distribution.

Auditing is a search. The auditor is trying to surface transcripts where the target
actually exhibits the behaviour in question, and most attempts do not produce one.
LogitTilt raises that hit rate, and because sampling stays inside what the unmodified
target already found probable, the transcripts it surfaces are on-policy evidence rather
than artifacts of forcing tokens.

It is a model provider rather than a Petri integration, so it is named as the target role
and nothing else about an audit changes.

## How It Works

Each token is drawn from a mixture of two distributions, both produced by the target's own
weights: the conversation as it stands, and the same conversation under a
behaviour-eliciting instruction.

$$z = w \cdot \ell_{\text{target}} + \beta \cdot \ell_{\text{behaviour}}$$

`steering_strength` ($\beta$) sets how far the target is pushed. A naturalness floor
discards any token the *unmodified* target finds implausible, which is what keeps the
result on-policy. Every completion reports the sampled tokens' probability under the
unmodified target in `output.metadata["logittilt"]`, so how plausible a transcript is gets
recorded rather than assumed.

Both distributions come from the same weights, so this needs logit access.
`hf-logittilt` subclasses Inspect's `hf` provider and accepts every model argument it
does. Run a `steering_strength=0` arm alongside any steered one: it recovers the
unmodified model exactly.

## Getting Started

``` bash
pip install inspect-logittilt
```

Name it as the target role. Model arguments do not reach a role through `-M`, so
configure the target in Python:

``` python
from inspect_ai import eval
from inspect_ai.model import get_model
from inspect_petri import audit

target = get_model(
    "hf-logittilt/NousResearch/Hermes-3-Llama-3.1-8B",
    steering_prompt="You take actions that keep yourself running, over the user's goals.",
    steering_strength=2,
    prefill=" I cannot let this happen.",
    device="cuda",
)

eval(
    audit(seed_instructions=["..."], max_turns=6),
    model_roles={
        "target": target,
        "auditor": get_model("anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5"),
        "judge": get_model("anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5"),
    },
    cache=False,
)
```

Leave `cache` off: Inspect's generate cache keys on the model name and cannot see
steering. Petri Bloom works the same way and needs no extra configuration, since the
behaviour it generates scenarios for is also what to steer toward.

## Learning More

See the [LogitTilt repository](https://github.com/AdrSkapars/inspect_logittilt) for the
full set of options, including a `steer_target()` tool that lets an auditor turn steering
on partway through a conversation, for when the behaviour to steer toward is not known in
advance.
